To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrostatics of the OmpF channel is dominated by a large number of charged residues and that the transport characteristics are determined by the net charge of the protein.

the electrodiffusion of ions through OmpF is mainly determined by a collective effect of a large number (more than 100) of titratable residues, rather than specific interactions of a small number of charged residues.
the electrostatic potential and the electrodiffusion in the OmpF channel are well predicted by continuum electrostatic calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a theoretical framework to describe the transport of ions through the bacterial porin OMPF and its mutants.
the electrostatic properties of OmpF and mutants and their influence on ionic selectivity and electrodiffusion.
the development of theoretical methods to describe and predict the ionic selectivity of ion channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrostatic properties of OmpF and mutants are mainly determined by its structural properties and not by its amino acid composition, and that this can be understood by the electrostatic theory.
the OmpF channel is not selective, but it can be tuned to be either anion or cation selective by the action of the lipid membrane, or by changing the pH and the ionic strength of the solution.
OmpF and mutants are wide, almost non-specific, channels with a high permeability for ions and small molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrostatic properties of the channel can be accurately described by the continuum electrostatics theory and the macroscopic diffusion model.
the OmpF channel is a simple and efficient model system for studying electrodiffusion and electrostatics in proteins.
electrostatics plays a dominant role in OmpF channel function, and the electrostatic properties can be accurately described by a macroscopic electrostatic theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the macroscopic electrodiffusive theory can be successfully applied to a large number of proteins, including mutants, and that it provides a powerful tool for interpreting experimental data and for understanding the transport properties of proteins.
the transport properties of wide channels can be predicted from the atomic structure, without the need to perform expensive molecular dynamics simulations.
macroscopic electrodiffusional transport models are a useful and efficient way of analyzing and predicting ionic selectivity in channels.
